h: Ham Radio License Exams, Online and In Person
docs.b: Ham Radio License Exams, Online and In Person PARC is an all-volunteer team of Volunteer Examiners. PARC helped pioneer remote video testing and offers examination sessions nearly every day. Same-day licensing is possible during FCC business hours, depending on FCC systems. Schedule an Exam Read the FAQ Welcome PARC is the longest continually operating online Volunteer Examiner (VE) team in the world. The detailed instructions on this website reflect the experience of tens of thousands of candidates, and the rules exist to protect the integrity of every examination. Candidates are expected to read the instructions and complete their preparation before the examination; PARC examiners assist with any remaining steps during the session. Candidates with concerns or special needs should contact PARC by email before booking. Online Exams Examinations are conducted from home over Zoom by a team of Volunteer Examiners. Careful preparation of the room and equipment is required. Online Testing In-Person Exams Sessions are held in Roanoke and Auburn, Alabama, and at other locations when published or by request. Photo identification and $15 in cash are required. In-Person Testing After Passing The CSCE, the FCC application fee, license issuance, and recommended next steps for new operators. What’s Next Projects & Mission PARC is an all-volunteer organization with members throughout the United States, known for administering amateur radio examinations nationwide. PARC is one of the three original groups authorized by the ARRL to pioneer remote video testing for amateur radio examinations. In addition to examinations, PARC provides training and presentations to community groups, youth groups and scouts. Members volunteer at Hamvention and Hamcation and provide communications and logistics support for community service projects, fundraisers and other events throughout the South. PARC also stands ready to support communities in disaster recovery. At Auburn University, PARC serves as VE Liaison for the testing sessions of the Auburn University Amateur Radio Club (AUARC), one of the oldest continually operating college radio clubs in the country, and provides training, education and technical support, including improvements to the club station. With Alpha Phi Omega, a national service fraternity founded on the principles of Scouting, PARC provides merit badge training to hundreds of scouts on campus each year, and assists other scout groups and organizations with JOTA (Jamboree on the Air) through public demonstrations of amateur radio. General Club Meeting The monthly club meeting is open to all, whether licensed or not, from new operators to experienced amateurs. When Third Thursday of each month Time 5:30 PM Central (1730) Where Online via Zoom Meeting ID 856-3271-4259 PARC Facebook group. PARC Telegram group: club and contest announcements.

docs.d: Book an amateur radio license exam with PARC. Sessions are available throughout the day and night and are reserved online.
docs.b: Schedule Your Exam Requirements Before Booking An FCC Registration Number (FRN), preferably registered with an email address other than Gmail (see the Gmail notice below). The same email address must be used to book, pay and register. The $15 examination fee is non-refundable; it is forwarded to the ARRL VEC. Candidates must read the online testing overview and the instructions before booking. Online Testing Overview Instructions Date of Birth Enter your date of birth to display the applicable session times. This step is optional. Your date of birth remains on your device. It is not sent to PARC or to Calendly and is not stored. It is used once, in your browser, to determine which times to display. Date of birth Month Select Day Select Year Select Show Available Times Prefer Not to Say Availability List Unavailable The combined calendar could not be loaded. Sessions can be booked directly on Calendly: Open All PARC Calendars on Calendly Time of day Times shown in your local time change ← → Available times: few several many — select a day to view its times. This calendar combines all PARC examination calendars, with duplicate start times merged. Selecting a time opens the Calendly booking form, which shows current availability. Notices Before Booking Gmail users must update the email address on their FRN before booking. FCC emails regarding the application fee are frequently not delivered to Gmail accounts, including to spam and junk folders. The FCC allows only 10 days for payment; after that period, it dismisses the application and the examination session is canceled. Once an application has been submitted, PARC examiners generally cannot resolve a missed FCC payment notice. Ensure that the FRN is registered with an email address other than Gmail before booking. Candidates must be fully prepared. Read the instructions and the FAQ before the examination. A candidate who is not ready when admitted is returned to the waiting room, and the next candidate is admitted. A second occurrence requires booking a new examination. Instructions FAQ Examination slots begin every 5 minutes. Most candidates finish in approximately 10 minutes; allow 15 minutes for the examination after setup. These figures are for planning purposes and are not time limits. Requests for additional time must be emailed before booking. After Booking A registration link is emailed within 48 hours and must be completed immediately. The Zoom link is emailed at least 45 minutes before the examination, and candidates join 45 minutes early. Prepare the room, computer and second device in the meantime. Prepare for Your Session

docs.t: Ham Radio Exam FAQ — Your Questions Answered
docs.d: Answers to the questions candidates ask most about online and in-person amateur radio license exams: fees, ID, equipment, rules, and results.
docs.b: Frequently Asked Questions Answers to the questions candidates ask most often, grouped by stage of the examination process. Select a question to display the answer. Contents Booking and Scheduling Payment Identification and Registration Equipment and Setup During the Exam After the Exam Accessibility and Accommodations Assistance with Costs Booking and Scheduling How do I schedule an exam? Online exams: select a time on the schedule. Candidates must read the online testing overview before booking. In-person exams: request an appointment by email, as described on the In-Person Testing page. Schedule Online Testing Overview In-Person Testing When will I receive the registration and Zoom links? Two emails are sent, both from vetesting@yahoo.com. The registration link is sent within 48 hours of booking; registrations are processed once a day, so candidates who book for the following day should continue to monitor their email. The registration must be completed as soon as it arrives: it is the license application (FCC Form 605), it requires the candidate’s FRN, and admission to the examination depends on it. The Zoom link is sent at least 45 minutes before the examination, and candidates join on both devices 45 minutes early. Check spam and junk folders for both emails. Can I take more than one exam in a session? Online exams: only when arranged by email before booking. Approval depends on practice test scores, the time required for each element, and the availability of consecutive time slots on the requested day. In-person exams: yes, provided that the first examination is completed within a reasonable time or additional examinations are requested from the exam team in advance. Two or Three Exams in One Session My session time has passed and I am still in the waiting room. What should I do? Remain in the waiting room. A candidate in the waiting room has received a link and is on the schedule. Sessions can run late when earlier candidates require more time, and the exam team admits each candidate as soon as possible. Monitor the Zoom chat for messages. Each device must display the candidate’s name followed by “computer” or “phone”; a device the team cannot identify is not admitted until all other candidates have been tested, if at all. No available time suits my schedule. What should I do? New times are added regularly; check the schedule again over the following days. If no suitable time becomes available, email vetesting@yahoo.com with the dates on which you are available and whether morning, afternoon or evening is preferred. Schedule Is there a time limit for the exam? Online exams: there is no strict time limit, although examination duration is recorded. Most prepared candidates finish in approximately 10 minutes; allow 15 minutes for the examination itself. If a candidate has missed more than 25% of the questions and the time taken indicates a lack of preparation, the exam team may end the examination. In-person exams: yes. Most exam teams remain at a session for up to one hour. Additional time must be requested from the exam team in advance. Because the examiners are volunteers, sufficient examiners may not be available beyond one hour; this varies by session. What happens if I miss my exam time slot? Candidates who need to reschedule must email PARC as soon as possible, so that the time slot can be offered to another candidate. A candidate who does not attend, or who does not give at least 24 hours’ notice, is recorded as a no-show. Payment What payment methods are accepted? Online exams: the $15 fee is paid by credit or debit card when booking a time slot on the schedule. There is no separate payment step. The same email address must be used for booking, payment and registration, or the session may not be matched to the payment. In-person exams: payment is made in cash at the session. PayPal is used only for donations, never for examination fees. Paying for Your Exam In-Person Testing Donations I paid for my exam but received a non-payment notice. What should I do? Either the card payment was not completed, or the name and email address on the payment do not match those on the examination registration. Request an invoice by email; it will be sent with your name in the subject line. What are donations used for? Donations are never required and are unrelated to booking an examination. They fund equipment, radio classes, internet service, subscriptions, power and training, including the infrastructure for online examinations. Neither club receives funding from a school or other organization; all funding comes from members and the wider amateur radio community. Support PARC Identification and Registration Does PARC give online exams to candidates who are not US citizens? Yes. Citizenship is not required, but a physical, unexpired US photo ID is: a state-issued driver’s license or photo ID card showing the candidate’s current residential address, or a US passport. Passports issued by other countries are not accepted for online examinations. Requirements for candidates under 18 are listed under Acceptable Identification. Do not book without acceptable identification: the examination cannot proceed without it, and the fee is not refunded. Acceptable Identification Is an FRN required? Yes. An FCC Registration Number (FRN) is required for all examinations. The FRN is issued by the FCC and requires identity verification. A Restricted Use FRN cannot be used. An FRN beginning with the digits 213 (among others) is a Restricted Use FRN, which cannot be used for an application in the Amateur Radio Service. A Restricted Use FRN may be used only on FCC Form 2100, Schedule 323-E (Ownership Report for Noncommercial Broadcast Stations). If an applicant attempts to use a Restricted Use FRN, the session is terminated and the examination is canceled for failure to provide a valid FRN. The applicant must obtain a standard FRN before scheduling another examination and applying for an amateur radio license. Do I need my PIN for the exam? No. The exam team requires only the candidate’s photo identification. The Exam Manager provides the code used to open the examination. How many forms of identification are required? Adult candidates require one: a physical state-issued driver’s license, state-issued photo ID card or US passport. Different requirements apply to candidates under 18. Acceptable Identification Equipment and Setup Are two devices with cameras required for an online exam? Yes. Two separate devices with working cameras, each with the Zoom application installed and running, are required for the entire session. Device requirements: Primary device (desktop or laptop computer) Must have a working camera. Must be positioned so that the camera provides a clear, unobstructed view of the candidate’s face from the computer screen. Is used for the Zoom meeting and the examination. Secondary device (phone, tablet or second computer) Requires its own working camera. Must be positioned at 90 degrees to the candidate’s left or right. The camera must provide a clear, continuous view of the entire workspace, including the candidate’s face, hands, keyboard, computer screen and surrounding area for the full duration of the examination. Both devices must remain connected to Zoom for the entire examination. The exam team has sole discretion to determine whether the camera setup meets these requirements. A candidate who does not meet these requirements will not be permitted to test and must attend an in-person session instead. Important: failure to set up the devices correctly or to follow any examination instruction results in forfeiture of the examination fee, without refund. There are no exceptions to the two-device requirement. The second camera must be placed directly to the left or right, not behind the candidate and not beside the screen. The examiners must be able to see the candidate’s hands and the screen at the same time. Can an iPad, tablet or Chromebook be used as the exam computer? Online exams: no. The candidate’s face must remain visible on camera throughout the examination, and these devices typically turn off the camera when sharing the screen. A laptop or desktop computer with a camera centered on the candidate’s face is required, together with the second camera device to one side. In-person exams: a device may be permitted if the exam team can confirm that it has no assistive software installed. This is at the discretion of the exam team. How are the devices renamed in Zoom? A device cannot be renamed in the waiting room; each device is named when joining. Sign out of the Zoom application on both devices first, because a signed-in device uses the account name and does not request a name. Then open the Zoom link from the email on each device and, when prompted, enter your first and last name followed by “computer” or “phone”, for example “Jane Doe computer”. The Zoom application is required; Zoom in a web browser is not supported. Naming the Devices Must the Zoom application be downloaded? Yes. The Zoom application must be installed and running on both devices. Zoom cannot be run from a web browser for the examination. Can a mouse or external keyboard be used? No. External mice and keyboards are not permitted on a laptop and are not required. Answers are selected with the A, B, C and D keys, which also advance the examination to the next question. Questions are aligned to the bottom of the window so that any diagrams above them remain visible. Minor adjustments during setup can be made with the trackpad; on a desktop computer, the mouse may be used during setup. How are Zoom settings tested? Install the Zoom application, then test video and audio using Zoom’s testing procedures. After confirming that audio and video work correctly, test the equipment in a Zoom test meeting. Zoom Testing Procedures Zoom Test Meeting Which applications may be running on the computer? To protect the integrity of the examination, all non-essential applications must be closed. These include, but are not limited to, mail, messaging, alerts, Teams, TeamViewer, Discord, Steam, VNC, remote desktop tools and VPNs. The exam team checks the computer for these applications. Running applications are shown by dots (Mac) or lines (Windows) beneath their icons in the taskbar or Dock; also check the hidden icons area (^) of the Windows taskbar, and quit everything not required to operate the computer. Follow the exam team’s instructions during setup. During the examination, only Zoom and the examination, in a single browser tab, may be open. Use the calculator built into ExamTools rather than a calculator application. Must wearable technology be removed? Yes. Headsets, earbuds, headphones, smart watches and smart glasses must be removed before joining Zoom and placed out of reach. Hats, wristbands and any item that could obscure the face or conceal an aid, such as a bandana or scarf, may not be worn. Can a multi-monitor setup be used? Only one monitor may be in operation in the room. A laptop may not be connected to a docking station. Remove, turn away or cover all additional screens or monitors; a shirt, blanket or towel is sufficient to cover a screen. During the examination, keep your attention on the examination screen. A bathroom is often a suitable location: it is small, has few electronic distractions, and the door can be locked. During the Exam Can I find out which questions I missed? Online exams: no. This information is not available to candidates. In-person exams: no. Examiners may disclose only the number of questions missed. Are the exam and the room recorded? Yes. When joining the meeting, candidates are asked to consent in accordance with recording laws. By consenting, the candidate confirms that any items they do not wish to be recorded during the examination or room scan have been covered or removed. A 360-degree scan of the room is required, together with a view of the work surface. The candidate agrees to the recording, storage and distribution of video, images and audio from the meeting. Recordings are kept for up to 30 days in case of any question about the exam protocol. PARC does not publish any information about candidates without their permission. Candidates may share their experience by leaving a review. Leave a Review After the Exam When is the CSCE issued? Online exams: by email within 48 hours. In-person exams: at the session, upon successful completion of an examination element. When will the FCC issue my call sign? PARC files electronically, so an upgrade, or a new license once the FCC’s $35 fee has been paid, can be granted the same day during FCC business hours. Issuance depends on FCC systems and usually takes up to 5–7 business days; backlogs can extend this. Wait ten business days before contacting PARC or the FCC. What’s Next Is a temporary license issued after passing? No. The CSCE records the elements passed, but a new operator may not transmit until the FCC grants the license and it appears in the FCC database. A new license is granted only after the FCC’s $35 application fee has been paid. Is any further action required after passing? Yes, for new licenses. The FCC charges a $35 fee for new amateur radio licenses, as mandated by Congress and in effect since April 19, 2022. After the first examination is passed, the Volunteer Examiner Coordinator submits the candidate’s information to the FCC. When the FCC processes the application, it emails instructions to pay the $35 fee online. The fee must be paid within 10 days or the application is dismissed; check spam folders for this email. There is currently no fee for address changes or upgrades. All other filings require a $35 fee. Accessibility and Accommodations Is a verbal exam available for candidates with special needs? Online exams: yes. A Volunteer Examiner designated by the exam team may read each question aloud, up to two times per question. In-person exams: yes. A Volunteer Examiner selected by the exam team may read the questions and answers aloud. May a person I know read the exam to me? No. This is strictly prohibited. Only Volunteer Examiners and candidates taking an examination may be present during the examination. The sole exception is that one parent may observe from a distance when the candidate is under age 13. I am unable to use an on-screen calculator. May I use scrap paper or a physical calculator? Online exams: no. Scrap paper and calculators other than the calculator built into ExamTools are not permitted. Candidates who cannot use it should consider an in-person examination and may email PARC to discuss the options. In-person exams: candidates may bring a basic calculator with no memory or programmable functions. Calculations are done on the back of the answer sheet. Accommodations How are accommodations arranged? Online exams: email PARC before booking with a description of the disability and the assistance required. For example, an examiner may read the questions aloud. Other accommodations depend on what can be provided while meeting the online examination requirements; some candidates are better served by an in-person session. In-person exams: reasonable accommodations can usually be provided, subject to the limitations of the location and at the sole discretion of the exam team. All examiners are volunteers and are under no obligation to administer an examination they are unable or unwilling to conduct. Accommodations Assistance with Costs Is financial assistance available to candidates age 17 or under? PARC is an officially recognized testing team for the ARRL VEC. Candidates who test with PARC may be eligible for the ARRL Youth Licensing Grant Program . In effect since April 19, 2022, the program covers the one-time $35 application fee for new amateur radio license candidates under 18 years of age who test under the ARRL Volunteer Examiner Coordinator (VEC) program . The program is funded by a special initiative that may be restricted or discontinued at any time . Until any change takes effect, eligible candidates who meet the requirements receive reimbursement. Candidates who did not test with the ARRL VEC, or who are over 17 years of age, are not eligible. After the examination, eligible candidates receive an email with a link to claim the reimbursement. ARRL Youth Licensing Grant Program How is an expired license reinstated? Within 728 days of expiration, a license can be renewed online through the FCC, or PARC can file the renewal for a fee. After that period, email an official copy of the expired license, or a copy of the official callbook page showing that the license was held before 1984, then schedule and pass the Technician class examination. Before the examination begins, inform the exam team that the license expired, that proof has been emailed, and that General, Advanced or Amateur Extra class privileges are to be restored. This cannot be processed after the examination without scheduling another examination. Further Assistance Common problems and their solutions are listed on the Troubleshooting page. PARC examiners are volunteers and cannot reply immediately. Email vetesting@yahoo.com and allow up to 24 hours for a reply, excluding holidays. Wait ten business days before contacting PARC or the FCC about license status. This is the normal processing time, and earlier inquiries do not shorten it. Retired members also answer questions in the PARC Facebook group. Troubleshooting Contact by Email PARC Facebook Group New Ham FAQ (PDF)

docs.t: In-Person Ham Radio Exams — Roanoke & Auburn, AL
docs.d: PARC gives in-person amateur radio license exams in Roanoke and Auburn, Alabama, plus other locations when published or by request.
docs.b: In-Person Exam Sessions PARC holds in-person examinations in Roanoke and Auburn, Alabama , and at other locations when published or by request. All sessions are by appointment; examiners travel to a session only when a candidate has a confirmed appointment. How In-Person Sessions Operate Examinations are administered under the ARRL Volunteer Examiner program, using the standard question pools for all amateur radio examinations. A published date indicates that at least three Volunteer Examiners are available that day. Sessions are not held without a booked candidate, so candidates must not travel to a session without a confirmed appointment . Sessions are held for any number of candidates, including a single candidate. Except at hamfests, a session is held only because a candidate has registered for it. Requests for a different date or time, or other special requests, may be accommodated where possible. Booking an Appointment Copy the lines below into an email to vetesting@yahoo.com and complete them. Specify the exact session , including the location, date and time. Name: Address: Mobile phone number: License class you want to take (Technician, General, Extra): Current call sign: Location you are registering for: Date & time of exam you are registering for: Special requests: Where possible, attach a recent photograph. Examiners use it to identify candidates at the session location. An appointment is confirmed only when PARC replies , normally within one day. If no reply is received, email again. Without a confirmed appointment, no examiners may be scheduled to attend, and the session may be canceled without notice. Items to Bring A government-issued photo ID. $15 in exact cash for each candidate. Change is not available. The ARRL sets the fee annually. A candidate who does not pass may be offered a different examination for an additional fee. For upgrades: the current license or any previously issued CSCE, and a copy to be retained by the examiners. An ink pen and a No. 2 pencil. A clipboard is recommended for outdoor sessions. Optionally, a basic calculator with no memory or programmable functions. Calculations are done on the back of the answer sheet. At the Session Most sessions are held at a table in a public place, such as a restaurant, away from other patrons where possible. Examiners are identified by an open black briefcase on the table. Restaurant staff may not be aware of the session. Candidates may eat and drink during the examination. Some sessions are held outdoors, and weather may change the date, time or location. Persons accompanying a candidate must wait in their vehicle, not at the session. Phones must be turned off completely and put away. Calls, texts and the use of a phone or smartwatch are not permitted during the examination. An examination takes from 5 minutes to half an hour. Examiners are normally available for up to one hour; requests for additional time, or for an additional element at the same session, must be made in advance. Examiners arrive at the specified time. In the event of a delay, examiners contact candidates by telephone or email. GPS coordinates for the location (DD.MM.MMM) are available on request. Candidates who pass receive their CSCE at the session. Time Zones Examination times are local to the testing location. Sessions in Alabama are held on Central Time, except in Valley, Alabama, which uses Eastern Time, as do all sessions in Georgia. Sessions in other states follow the local time of the testing location. Changes and Cancellations Notify PARC as early as possible, and at least 24 hours in advance, if an appointment cannot be kept. Examiners cannot all be contacted on the day of a session, and a candidate may be the only person scheduled. Study Resources All questions are drawn from the published question pools maintained by the NCVEC. The following resources provide the question pools and practice examinations: Where and How to Study ARRL Question Pools eHam Practice Exams HamExam.org HamTesting.com QRZ Practice Tests About the Team PARC has administered examinations to new and experienced amateur radio operators for many years. The group began with one family, a husband, wife and three sons, and now includes volunteers in Roanoke, Valley, Alexander City, Auburn, Anniston and Huntsville, Alabama, and in Columbus and LaGrange, Georgia. PARC also conducts testing at Southern Union and Auburn University. Every team member holds an Amateur Extra class license and is qualified to administer examinations for all license classes. PARC also assists with testing nationwide and is registered with several Volunteer Examiner Coordinators, including ARRL, W5YI, CAVEC, Alaska and Laurel. Classes and examinations are available on request, in addition to the regularly scheduled sessions in Alabama and Georgia. All team members serve as volunteers. Online Testing from Home

docs.d: Everything required for a remote video amateur radio exam with PARC. Read all instructions and requirements before paying or registering.
docs.b: Online Testing PARC conducts video-supervised examinations nearly every day of the week. Candidates test from home on their own computers, supervised over Zoom by a team of at least three Volunteer Examiners. Requirements An FCC Registration Number (FRN) , not an FCC username, obtained before booking. The FRN should be registered with an email address other than Gmail. A license cannot be issued without an FRN. Two devices with cameras : a computer for the examination, and a phone or tablet on a stand beside the candidate, at ninety degrees, showing the candidate, both hands and the screen. A Windows or Mac laptop or desktop computer . Chromebooks, iPads and other tablets cannot run the examination. A quiet, private room with the door closed and a clear desk. A physical photo ID , as listed under Acceptable Identification. Read the Instructions See Available Times Acceptable Identification From Booking to License The complete process, in order: Booking Select a time on the schedule. The $15 fee is paid when booking; there is no separate payment step. Use the same email address for every step that follows. Registration A registration link is emailed within 48 hours. Registrations are processed once a day, so candidates who book for the following day should monitor their email, including spam folders. Complete the registration immediately; it is the FCC license application. Preparation Prepare the room, computer, second device and identification, using the pre-exam checklist. Joining the Session The Zoom link is emailed at least 45 minutes before the examination. Join on both devices 45 minutes early and remain in the waiting room until admitted. Sessions may run late; a candidate in the waiting room remains on the schedule. Check-In Present photo identification (requirements differ for candidates under 18), then scan the room slowly with the second camera so that the team can see the entire workspace. The Examination Questions appear on the screen and are answered with the A, B, C and D keys. There is no strict time limit; most prepared candidates finish in approximately ten minutes. Results The team grades the examination during the session and reports the result before the candidate leaves. The CSCE, which records the elements passed, is emailed within 48 hours. FCC Application Fee For a new license, the FCC emails instructions for its $35 application fee. Payment is due within 10 days, or the FCC dismisses the application. Upgrades do not require a fee. License Issuance PARC files electronically, so a license can be granted the same day during FCC business hours. Issuance depends on FCC systems and can take up to 5–7 business days. docs.b: Online Exam Instructions Choose an Instruction Format Step-by-Step Instructions One step per page, with a Next button at the end of each page. Complete Text Instructions All steps on this page, below, for reading in full or printing. Candidates new to online examinations should first read the overview. Online Testing Overview Contents Before You Book an Online Exam Where and How to Study How to Book, Pay and Register Your situation Acceptable Identification Preparing Your Room Preparing Your Computer Preparing Your Second Device Rules for Online Exams Exam Day Protocol CSCE and FCC Form 605 This page contains the complete requirements for online examinations. Select a section above to go directly to it. Pre-Exam Checklist The same requirements as a printable checklist. Before You Book an Online Exam Online examinations are supervised live over Zoom by a team of at least three Volunteer Examiners, one candidate at a time. PARC conducts these examinations with the permission of the ARRL VEC and the FCC, under strict rules that protect the integrity of every result. Requirements Two devices with cameras , both connected to Zoom for the entire session: a Windows or Mac computer for the examination, and a phone or tablet positioned beside the candidate to show the candidate, both hands and the screen. A private, quiet room with a door that closes and no other persons present. Consent to a room scan and a recording. The entire room is shown on camera, and the session is recorded. Remove or cover any items that should not be recorded. An FCC Registration Number (FRN) before booking. The FRN should be registered with an email address other than Gmail, because FCC fee notices are frequently not delivered to Gmail accounts. A physical photo ID from the list of acceptable identification. Candidates who cannot meet these requirements, or who do not consent to the room scan and recording, should schedule an in-person session. Acceptable Identification In-Person Sessions Candidates must be fully prepared. A candidate who is not ready when admitted is returned to the waiting room, and the next candidate is admitted. A second occurrence requires booking a new examination. Where and How to Study Book an examination only after consistently scoring 85% or higher on at least 15 practice tests . Each session requires the time of several volunteers and a time slot that could otherwise be assigned to another candidate. Practice Tests and Classes HamStudy.org Free practice tests and a study mode that tracks progress, with an optional low-cost mobile application. ARRL Exam Review Free practice examinations from the ARRL, the national association for amateur radio. New England Sci-Tech Online license classes recommended by PARC examiners. Study with Ham Radio Prep Ham Radio Prep provides an interactive online license course of videos, text lessons, quizzes and games. The course has had more than 60,000 successful students and offers a 100% money-back guarantee to students who do not pass on the first attempt. Coupon code PARC provides an additional 20% discount . The following links apply the code automatically: Technician Course General Course Amateur Extra Course Tech + General Bundle All Access License Pass Alternatively, register at HamRadioPrep.com and enter code PARC at checkout. HamRadioPrep.com How to Book, Pay and Register All candidates book the same way. Some situations require arrangements before booking, so review the situations listed at the end of this page first. 1. Book and Pay Select a time on the schedule. The $15 examination fee is paid by card when booking. There is no separate payment step. Use the same email address to book, pay and register. A different address is the most common reason a booking cannot be matched to its payment. The fee is forwarded to the ARRL VEC and is non-refundable, including for missed examinations and equipment failures. Candidates who do not pass may book another session, including on the same day. Each attempt requires a separate $15 fee. Go to the Schedule 2. Register A registration link is emailed from vetesting@yahoo.com within 48 hours of booking. Registrations are processed once a day; candidates who book for the following day should monitor their email, including spam and junk folders. Complete the registration as soon as it arrives. The registration is the license application (FCC Form 605), and it is required for admission to the examination. Enter your name exactly as it appears on your photo identification. Upgrade candidates must email a copy of their current license, or of any CSCE from a previous session, as a PDF to vetesting@yahoo.com before registering. Basic qualification question. The application includes the FCC basic qualification (felony) question. A candidate who answers yes must send the required documentation directly to the FCC within 14 days of the filing date, referencing the application file number, as described by the ARRL. Otherwise, the FCC dismisses the application. This documentation must not be sent to PARC or the VEC. ARRL: FCC Qualification Question Public Record of the License Address The name and mailing address on a license become public when the license is issued. Telephone numbers, email addresses and Social Security numbers are not published. To list a PO Box on the application, email your physical address to vetesting@yahoo.com before registering, with the subject line “Physical Address for Non-Public Record Only” and the reason for the request. Email a PO Box Request ARRL: Licensee Privacy Your situation One Exam One examination element in one session. This is the standard booking, and no advance arrangement is required. Book a single time slot on the schedule. A candidate who passes and wishes to attempt the next element on the same day may ask the examiner during the session. This is possible only when the adjacent time slots are available. Two or Three Exams in One Session Two or three examination elements taken consecutively in one session, such as Technician and General on the same day. This must be arranged before booking . Each Zoom session must serve as many candidates as possible, and additional elements occupy time slots reserved for other candidates. Approval depends on the candidate’s practice test scores, the time required for each element, and the availability of consecutive time slots on the requested day. More Than One Candidate in the Same Building Two or more candidates testing from the same residence or building. Each candidate requires a separate booking, computer, second device and room. Candidates may not share a screen, desk or room. The room scan and camera requirements apply to each candidate individually, exactly as they would to a candidate testing alone. Candidates may book simultaneous time slots, provided that each candidate meets these requirements. Accommodations Candidates whose disability requires an adjustment to the standard examination procedure may request an accommodation. Any change to the standard procedure requires approval in advance. Some accommodations require a different session type or an additional examiner, and cannot be arranged on the day of the examination. For example, an examiner may read each question aloud, up to two times, during an online examination. Wider support is available to licensed and prospective amateur radio operators with disabilities. Accessible Testing and HandiHam Acceptable Identification Identification is presented to the camera, front and back, until every examiner has verified it. The physical document is required. Mobile or digital IDs, photographs and copies are not accepted. Adult Candidates One unexpired photo ID from the following list: State-issued driver’s license State-issued photo ID card US passport. Passports issued by other countries are not accepted. A driver’s license or state ID must show the candidate’s current residential address. Business addresses, PO Boxes and mail services are not accepted. United States citizenship is not required, but one of these documents is. Candidates Under 18 With a photo ID from the list above, no further identification is required. Without a photo ID , a parent or legal guardian must appear on camera, present their own photo ID from the list above, and verbally identify themselves and the candidate. The candidate must then present one of the following: Non-photo state ID card (issued by some states) Birth certificate bearing the official seal Social Security card Minor’s work permit School ID card School or public library card Report cards are not accepted. Candidates Age 13 and Under Age 13 and under: before the examination, a parent must complete the COPPA consent form and email it to the address on the form. Under age 13: an adult must remain in the room during the examination. COPPA Consent Form (PDF) An examination cannot proceed without acceptable identification, and the fee is not refunded. Candidates who are uncertain whether their identification qualifies should email vetesting@yahoo.com before booking. Preparing Your Room Each numbered item stops the session. The examiner will require the desk to be cleared or the examination to be rescheduled. One screen, the second device at ninety degrees, and the identification. No other items on the surface or within reach. Room Selection Use a room with a door that closes, where no one will enter during the examination. A bathroom or a large closet is often suitable because it is small, quiet and easy to clear. Vehicles, outdoor locations and any location with uncontrollable noise are not permitted. Sit at a desk, table or counter, on a stable chair that does not rock or recline. Beds and couches are not permitted. Clearing the Room and Desk Remove anything that could assist with the examination or appear to do so: notes, books, papers and sticky notes, calculators, additional screens and other electronic devices, and any amateur radio items, such as radios, posters and QSL cards. Clear the desk and the surrounding floor of all items not required for the examination, including food and drinks, headphones, waste baskets, vapes, ashtrays and tobacco products. Open closet doors and shower curtains for the room scan, and close them before the examination begins. Other Persons and Animals No other persons or animals may be present in the room. The only exceptions are a service dog and the adult required to remain with a candidate under age 13, as described under Acceptable Identification. Instruct household members not to enter the room and to avoid noise, including from pets, during the examination. If anyone enters the room, the examination must be stopped. Acceptable Identification Preparing Your Computer Computer Requirements A Windows 10 (or later) or Mac laptop or desktop computer. Chromebooks, iPads and other tablets, and Linux computers are not permitted. A camera facing the candidate directly and a working microphone. On a laptop, use the built-in camera. Reliable internet service. VPNs and phone hotspots are not permitted. One screen. Turn off, turn away or cover any additional monitors, and disable virtual screens. A laptop may not be connected to a docking station. Keyboard and mouse. A laptop must use only its built-in keyboard and trackpad; external mice and keyboards are not permitted. A desktop computer requires a wired keyboard and mouse. The computer must be fully charged or connected to power. Zoom Setup Install the Zoom application on the computer and the phone. Zoom in a web browser is not supported. Test both devices before the day of the examination, and become familiar with the use of Zoom. Virtual backgrounds and background blur are not permitted. The examiners must be able to see the entire room. Zoom Test Meeting Naming the Devices The examiners admit devices by name. Each device name must consist of the candidate’s first and last name followed by “computer” or “phone”. Sign out of Zoom on both devices. When signed in, Zoom uses the account name and does not request a name. Open the Zoom link from the email on each device. When Zoom requests a name, enter your first and last name followed by computer or phone . Devices cannot be renamed in the waiting room. On the computer, turn on video and join audio with the microphone unmuted. On the phone, turn on video but do not join audio, as described under Preparing Your Second Device. Before Joining Close all applications except Zoom, including browsers, email, messaging, Teams, Discord, Steam, remote-desktop tools and VPNs. Turn on Do Not Disturb and turn off Bluetooth. A notification that appears during the examination may be taken as outside assistance, and the examiners are required to act on it. Remove watches, earbuds, headphones, smart glasses and hats, and place them out of reach. Do Not Disturb, called Focus on newer Macs and on iPhones, is indicated by this moon symbol. On a Mac, Do Not Disturb and Bluetooth are located in Control Center, shown by this icon at the top right of the menu bar. Examination Window The browser window must not be maximized or full screen. Part of the desktop must remain visible on every side, so that the examiners can confirm that nothing else is open. The examination runs in a browser window, which the Exam Manager instructs you to open after your screen is shared. Before the day of the examination, practice sizing a browser window as shown, and then close it. Answer using the A, B, C and D keys ; the next question appears automatically. Do not scroll or touch the trackpad during the examination. Use only the calculator built into ExamTools . A separate calculator application, or a physical calculator in the room, is grounds for ending the examination. Preparing Your Second Device The phone or tablet serves as the examiners’ second camera. It is used to scan the room and then remains positioned beside the candidate for the entire examination. The second camera must be placed directly to the left or right, not behind the candidate and not beside the screen. The examiners must be able to see the candidate’s hands and the screen at the same time. Placement Place the device on a stand directly to your left or right , near the front edge of the desk, at a distance that shows your face, both hands, the keyboard and the screen. The device may not lie flat. Position the device horizontally and use the rear camera . Practice switching from the front camera before the day of the examination. Where possible, keep the door within view of one of the cameras. The required view: the keyboard and the screen from the side, with the candidate and both hands visible. The device must be positioned horizontally. A stand or clip mount holds it steady. Device Requirements A phone or tablet with a working camera, an internet connection and the Zoom application installed. Fully charged or connected to power for the entire session. A phone stand or clip mount. Audio Settings Before the day of the examination, set Zoom on the device not to join audio automatically. When the device joins the session, do not join audio . On an iPhone, select “Cancel”; on other devices, select “Deny” or “Dial by phone,” or make no selection. Muting is not sufficient, because two devices with audio connected cause feedback. When the team admits the phone to the session, place it down and do not touch it , regardless of what appears on its screen. The team moves the device in and out of the session to disconnect its audio, which is effective on most phones. Keep your attention on the computer until the team instructs you to pick up the phone. Handling the phone can cause feedback, which may require disconnecting all devices and rejoining after the next candidate. Rules for Online Exams These rules protect the integrity of every examination result. A violation may end the examination, and the fee is not refunded. Prohibited Equipment Paper, pens or pencils Calculators, whether physical devices or applications (the calculator built into ExamTools is permitted) More than one screen iPads and other tablets, Chromebooks and Linux computers (Windows or Mac only) Bluetooth devices of any kind External keyboards or mice connected to a laptop, and docking stations Items That May Not Be Worn Watches, smart glasses and any other electronic devices Earbuds, AirPods, headphones, neck loops, or any other device in or over the ears Sunglasses or polarized glasses Hats or caps Items Not Permitted in the Room Other persons or animals, except as described under Preparing Your Room Any amateur radio materials, including charts, formulas and notes Papers of any kind, including notepads and examination instructions Food or drinks Cameras, external microphones, smart speakers such as HomePods, or unusual wiring Conduct During the Exam Keep your eyes on the screen and both hands on the keyboard area, within view of the phone camera. Talking, reading the questions aloud and mouthing the words are prohibited, even without sound. Keep the computer camera and microphone operating throughout the examination. Circumstances in Which an Exam Cannot Proceed The candidate cannot present acceptable identification. The fee is not refunded. The candidate is outdoors, in a vehicle of any kind (moving or parked), or in any location other than a room that can be secured. The location is noisy, for example because of children, machinery or traffic. Noise interferes with the examination and the examiners even when it does not disturb the candidate. Arrange for childcare or another location, or schedule an in-person session. Acceptable Identification Preparing Your Room In-Person Sessions Exam Day Protocol The Exam Manager reads this protocol at the start of the examination, and the candidate must agree to it. Review it before the day of the examination. Before Admission The Zoom link is emailed at least 45 minutes before the examination. Check spam and junk folders. Join on both devices 45 minutes before the examination and remain in the waiting room. A candidate in the waiting room is on the schedule, even when the session is running late. Screen sharing and other Zoom features must not be tested in the waiting room. Doing so results in removal from the session. Candidate Agreement The parent or guardian of a child candidate must be present for this part of the protocol and must answer the questions. You must complete the examination without any interruption that could raise doubts about the integrity of the testing environment. You are asked to complete the examination within your assigned 15-minute time block, which is sufficient for most candidates. You must keep your attention on the computer screen at all times. Your eyes may not wander to other parts of the room, and you may not leave your seat. You may not read the questions or answers aloud or talk to yourself. Mouthing the words counts as talking, even without sound. Drinks, snacks and any other items that could distract you must be removed from the testing area. Visitors and pets may not enter the room; the doors must be closed and locked. You will scan the room with the phone camera to show that nothing could assist you, and then position the phone so that it shows you, the keyboard and both hands. Scrap paper, calculators and all other assistance are prohibited; use the calculator built into ExamTools. All browsers, email and note applications must be quit completely, leaving only the Zoom application open. You must agree to share your entire screen with the exam team, not only a browser window. You must agree that the session is recorded and stored for up to 30 days in case of any question about a breach of the exam protocol. You must agree that if the exam team suspects cheating , the examination may be terminated, the fee forfeited, and you may be barred from future online examinations. Examination Procedure Present your photo identification, front and back, to the camera until every examiner has verified it. The Exam Manager starts recording your screen, webcam and phone camera. Using the phone camera, step back to show the computer and workspace, then scan the room: the walls and floor, under the table and chair, under the laptop and keyboard, followed by a close-up of the computer, keyboard, hands and arms. Position the phone at a distance, aimed at the computer, so that it shows you, your hands and the computer. Share your full desktop in Zoom, not only a browser window: select the green Share Screen button at the bottom of the window, then the blue Share button in the pop-up window. Open a browser window in the center of the screen (the examination questions are approximately 4 inches wide) and show that nothing else is open. Open Display Settings to show that only one screen is in use. Enter the address provided by the Exam Manager, select Join Exam Session , and enter the session call sign, KJ4PJE , and the 4-digit code provided by the Exam Manager . The Exam Manager opens the examination. Verify your name, address and telephone number at this point. They cannot be changed later; any change after the examination voids it. The examiners turn off their video and microphones, and the examination begins. Keep your attention on the screen and your camera and microphone on. The right arrow key advances to the next question. When finished, select Grade Exam , at the bottom of the page or at the top right. The score is displayed; the specific questions missed cannot be shown. Select Finish and Sign Forms , verify your name and address, and sign electronically to complete the application and CSCE. The forms are shown on the next page. Select Finish Session , then Logout . The Exam Manager stops the recording and ends the screen share. After the Exam The CSCE (Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination) is emailed within 48 hours. The application and scores are uploaded that evening, so a license may appear in the FCC database the same day during FCC business hours, or within approximately 5–7 business days. New licenses are granted only after the FCC’s $35 application fee is paid. The FCC emails payment instructions, and payment is due within 10 days. The Exam Manager recommends joining a local radio club and the ARRL, and explains how to contact PARC or AUARC regarding examinations and training. For online training, PARC recommends New England Sci-Tech and can provide a referral. Leave the session by selecting the red Leave button at the bottom right of the screen. The Exam Manager may disconnect the candidate instead. CSCE and FCC Form 605 What’s Next CSCE and FCC Form 605 At the end of the examination, candidates sign two documents: the license application (FCC Form 605) and the CSCE (Certificate of Successful Completion of Examination), which records the elements passed. This page shows each screen so that personal details can be verified in advance. 1. Verification of Personal Details When the examination opens, confirm your full legal name, address, telephone number and email address. Your name must match your photo identification exactly. Details can be changed only at this point; any change after the examination requires voiding the examination and starting again. 2. Review of the Forms The signing page. The two blue boxes open the forms, which are completed from the details confirmed at the start of the examination. The first box, Review Quick Form 605 , opens the application: The second box, Review CSCE , opens the certificate: Candidates may ask to review either form before signing. 3. Certification Signing the certification confirms agreement with each of its statements: The CSCE is emailed within 48 hours. Book Your Exam Select a time on the schedule. After the examination, refer to What’s Next. Book Your Exam What’s Next

docs.b: What’s Next After Passing Your Exam This page describes the steps between a successful examination and the issuance of a license, followed by recommended next steps for new operators. New License Upgrade Getting Started Restoring Your Computer Leave a Review Do not change any FCC records for 30 days after a license or upgrade is granted , including the address, name or email address, and do not apply for a vanity call sign during that period. New License: FCC Application Fee FCC email. When the FCC begins processing the application, it emails payment instructions to the address on the Form 605. FCC email is frequently not delivered to Gmail accounts; check spam and junk folders. FCC CORES. Beginning two business days after the examination, log in to FCC CORES to locate the application and the payment option, whether or not an email has arrived. Payment within 10 days. Pay the $35 fee following the FCC’s payment instructions. If the fee is not paid in time, the FCC dismisses the application and the process must be repeated. New licenses are issued in order of payment. FCC CORES Login FCC Payment Instructions Candidates under 18 who tested with PARC may be eligible for reimbursement of the fee through the ARRL Youth Licensing Grant Program. ARRL Youth Licensing Grant Upgrade: No Fee The FCC does not currently charge a fee for upgrades. Fees apply only to new licenses, renewals and call sign changes. An upgrade is processed once any required verification is complete. All Candidates Felony conviction. Submit the required documentation directly to the FCC. This process is strictly between the candidate and the FCC; PARC cannot assist or intervene. Processing time. A call sign may appear in the FCC ULS database within days, or within several weeks when the FCC has a backlog, such as after system outages or a government shutdown. Contacts: If no FCC email has been received ten days after the examination, email vetesting@yahoo.com , and PARC will check the status of the application. If the fee has been paid and no license has appeared ten days after payment, call the FCC at (888) 225-5322. Otherwise, do not contact the FCC, the ARRL or PARC about the application. The FCC’s call center is operated by a contractor and may not have accurate information. Licensing During a Government Shutdown Getting Started New operators are encouraged to continue learning and to take part in the amateur radio community. Join a local amateur radio club. Attend hamfests and local events. Consider membership in the ARRL for resources and advocacy. Before purchasing equipment, learn what other operators in the area use. Low-cost handheld radios such as Baofeng or Wouxun can be difficult to program and have limited range. Equipment reviews are a useful reference. PARC Radio & Technology holds a monthly meeting on Zoom with amateur radio news, technical tips and a presentation on a topic of interest. New operators are welcome to attend in addition to their local club. Find an ARRL Club ARRL eHam Equipment Reviews PARC Meeting Details QRZ Jumpstart Program: $17.99 Radio Offer New licensees may receive a one-time 70% discount on a QRZ-1 radio. Applications must be submitted within six months of the license issue date: Create a QRZ account after the call sign has been issued. Submit the Jumpstart application. Apply the discount code sent by QRZ to a QRZ-1 radio and accessories. Create a QRZ Account Jumpstart Application Program Details (GigaParts) PARC Telegram Group PARC uses Telegram for club and contest announcements. Members must configure their profiles as follows: Name: the name you go by, followed by your call sign — for example, Gary K4XYZ . The last name field may be left blank. Username: @Firstname_Callsign — for example, @Gary_K4XYZ . This allows members to find you without your telephone number. Profile photos: visible to Everybody. Join the Telegram Group Telegram Setup Instructions Install Telegram from the App Store (iPhone) or Google Play (Android) by searching for Telegram Messenger, or download the desktop application from telegram.org. Create an account. Open Telegram, select Start Messaging, and enter your mobile number and the verification code sent by text message. Set the name in the format shown above when prompted. To change it later: Settings → select your name → Edit. Set the username: Settings → Username → enter it in the format shown above → Save. Set profile photo visibility: Settings → Privacy and Security → Profile Photos → Everybody. Restrict telephone number visibility (recommended): Settings → Privacy and Security → Phone Number. Set “Who can see my phone number” to Nobody and “Who can find me by my number” to My Contacts. Join the group using the button above. If you are signed in to Telegram, the group opens automatically. For assistance, contact a PARC volunteer. PARC also maintains a Facebook group. PARC Facebook Group Upgrading Your License Each higher license class adds operating privileges and frequency allocations. Book the Next Element Upgrade examinations are booked on the schedule in the same way as the first examination. Book Your Next Exam Study for the Next License with Ham Radio Prep Ham Radio Prep provides an interactive online license course of videos, text lessons, quizzes and games. The course has had more than 60,000 successful students and offers a 100% money-back guarantee to students who do not pass on the first attempt. Coupon code PARC provides an additional 20% discount . The following links apply the code automatically: Technician Course General Course Amateur Extra Course Tech + General Bundle All Access License Pass Alternatively, register at HamRadioPrep.com and enter code PARC at checkout. HamRadioPrep.com Restoring Your Computer After the Exam Preparing for the examination involved changing settings and closing programs. Shut the computer down completely and restart it. This restores normal startup programs, including the system tray on Windows and Finder and the menu bar on a Mac. All Computers Browser: close the window used for the examination. Bluetooth: turn it back on if it is normally used. Do Not Disturb or Focus: turn it off. Windows Desktop icons: right-click the desktop → View → Show desktop icons . Mac Desktop icons: restore the normal desktop icon display. Stacks: click the desktop → View → clear Use Stacks if individual icons are normally shown. Applications: reopen any applications that were force-quit for the examination.

docs.t: FCC Fees & Licensing During a Government Shutdown
docs.d: How a federal government shutdown affects FCC CORES payments, application processing, and your new amateur radio license or upgrade.
h: Effect of a Shutdown on Licensing
How to Pay the $35 Application Fee in CORES
docs.b: Licensing During a Government Shutdown The most recent shutdown ended in November 2025, and the FCC has resumed normal operations. This page remains available because its guidance applies to any future shutdown. Current processing information is provided under What’s Next. What’s Next Effect of a Shutdown on Licensing During a government shutdown, the FCC does not process license applications. When the FCC reopens, its systems are heavily backlogged. Applications are processed in order of examination date, so it may take several weeks before an application appears in the FCC database. The FCC licensing system is a legacy platform with known stability issues, maintained by a small number of qualified personnel. Outages and slow processing are likely after a shutdown, and recovery from a system failure can take several days. Required Actions Obtain a valid FRN. A candidate who tested without an FRN, or with ten zeroes in place of one, must obtain an FRN before the examination can be submitted to the FCC. Each person receives only one FRN; an FRN issued for any previous FCC license remains that person’s FRN. Obtain the FRN from FCC CORES as soon as possible (instructions below), then email it to vetesting@yahoo.com with the subject line formatted exactly as follows, using your own number and name: FRN - 0031234567 - First Name Last Name . PARC then updates the paperwork and submits the application, and processing time is counted from that date. Pay the $35 license fee as soon as the FCC system allows , to retain the application’s place in the queue. The FCC emails payment instructions to the address on the Form 605 when processing begins; check spam and junk folders regularly. An application is dismissed if the email is missed or the fee is paid late, and the process must then be repeated. Felony documentation. A candidate with a felony conviction must submit the required documentation as soon as FCC systems are available. This process is strictly between the candidate and the FCC; PARC cannot assist or intervene. Contact. Do not contact the FCC, the ARRL or PARC about the application while FCC systems recover. The FCC call center is operated by a contractor and may not have accurate information. How to Obtain an FRN Go to the FCC CORES website by searching for “FCC CORES Login.” Select “Register” or “Create an Account.” Enter an email address and create a password. After signing in, select “Register for a New FRN.” Select “Individual.” Enter your name and contact information. Submit the form. The new FRN appears on the confirmation page. Record it for future use. How to Pay the $35 Application Fee in CORES Sign in to FCC CORES with your email address and password. On the main page, select “Submit a New Filing.” Select “ULS Application Fee.” Enter your FRN and confirm your information. Select the $35 Amateur Radio License Fee. Follow the prompts to pay by credit card or bank transfer. Save or print the payment confirmation for your records. Expected Processing After the FCC reopens, licenses are issued in order of examination date, once payment and any required verification are complete. A call sign may appear in the FCC ULS database within days, or within several weeks, depending on the backlog. An application that has been paid but does not appear after several weeks is most likely still in the queue. Getting Started After Licensing

h: Amateur Radio for People with Disabilities
docs.b: Amateur Radio for People with Disabilities Amateur radio is open to everyone, regardless of physical ability, hearing or vision. It provides a means to communicate with others, develop technical skills, and participate in a worldwide network of operators. PARC supports HandiHam, a long-established organization that helps people with disabilities take part in and succeed in amateur radio. This includes people who are blind, deaf or hard of hearing, or physically impaired, and people with other conditions that make learning or operating a radio more difficult. HandiHam.org Getting Started Amateur radio is more accessible than ever. Voice modes, digital modes and Morse code offer options for every operator. Many tools and radios are compatible with, or can be adapted to, assistive technologies such as screen readers, speech-to-text software and adaptive keyboards. Full use of the hands, hearing or eyesight is not required to operate a radio. Radios can be operated with foot pedals, speech recognition, braille displays and sip-and-puff devices, and operators who do not speak can communicate using keyboards and text-based modes. Studying for the Exam PARC can refer candidates with disabilities to study resources, including: Audio and braille study guides Online courses compatible with screen readers Video content with captions and sign language One-to-one support from mentors and volunteers Taking the Exam Candidates who require assistance or accommodations must submit a request before booking. PARC works with the Volunteer Examiner team to provide the support required. Verbal Examinations Online: an examiner may read each question aloud, up to two times. This must be requested in advance, with the reason for the request. Additional time is allowed when the questions are read to the candidate. In person: an examiner may read the entire examination aloud. Up to one hour is allowed. Assistance from Others Another person may assist with setup before the examination begins, but must leave before it starts. Only examiners may be present during the examination. The sole exception is a parent, who may observe from a distance when the candidate is under age 13. Calculators Online: only the calculator built into ExamTools is permitted. A candidate who cannot use it should consider an in-person examination. In person: candidates may bring a basic calculator with no memory or programmable functions. Calculations are done on the back of the answer sheet. Examination Results Candidates are told the number of questions missed. The specific questions missed are not disclosed. Online Examination Requirements An unexpired physical photo ID, as listed under Acceptable Identification. An FCC Registration Number (FRN), obtained before booking. A quiet, private room, not a vehicle or an outdoor location, with a clear desk and no distracting items in view. Sharing the full screen and scanning the room over Zoom. Candidates who do not consent to this should choose an in-person examination. Acceptable Identification In-Person Sessions Contact For information or assistance, email vetesting@yahoo.com . PARC will refer the request to a volunteer familiar with the candidate’s needs. PARC examiners are unpaid volunteers; allow up to 24 hours for a reply. Assistance is also available through the PARC Facebook group. PARC Facebook Group Testing with PARC Requests for accommodations must be made before booking. docs.b: How to Book, Pay and Register All candidates book the same way. Some situations require arrangements before booking, so review the situations listed at the end of this page first. 1.
